Where it began

Alex Hales was born in Hillingdon on 3 January 1989 and went to school at Westbrook Hay and then Chesham, in Buckinghamshire. He first made people sit up in 2005, at a youth Twenty20 event at Lord's, when the sixteen-year-old took 55 runs from a single over. He had been picked as a fast bowler.

He played Minor Counties cricket for Buckinghamshire, then went on trial at Nottinghamshire in 2007 and made 218 in only his second game for them. Notts signed him, and Trent Bridge became his home ground for years to come.

The player

He was a right-handed opener who liked to hit the ball very hard and very far. In the 2014 World Twenty20 he made 116 not out against Sri Lanka, the first hundred by an England batter in a Twenty20 international. Two summers later, at Trent Bridge, he hit 171 against Pakistan, then the highest one-day innings ever played for England, as the side piled up 444 for 3.

His Test career came between December 2015 and 2016: 11 matches, 573 runs at 27.29 and five fifties. The best of them came at Lord's against Sri Lanka in 2016, when he made 94 before Angelo Mathews trapped him six runs short of the honours board.

What made him special

Power and timing, mostly, and the nerve to use them from the first ball. His finest night came in the 2022 T20 World Cup, when he was called into the squad late. He and Jos Buttler put on 170 without loss against India in the semi-final, Hales finishing on 86 not out as man of the match, and England went on to lift the trophy.

Test cricket, with its slips waiting patiently, asked trickier questions of his game, and the hundred never quite came. He did, though, collect a set of near misses few can match: he was the first batter to be out for 99 in both a one-day international and a Twenty20 international.

Away from the middle

He retired from international cricket in August 2023 and took his big hitting around the world's Twenty20 leagues. He was the leading run-scorer in the 2020-21 Big Bash for the Sydney Thunder, turned out for the Trent Rockets in each of The Hundred's first four summers, and in 2025 won the Caribbean Premier League with the Trinbago Knight Riders.

And finally

Sport runs in the family. His grandfather Dennis was a fine tennis player who once took Rod Laver to five sets at Wimbledon. Alex, sensibly, chose a game where hitting the ball out of the ground is the whole idea.
